current_activity: Market Garden: corps headquarters lands by glider and sets up near Groesbeek; no contact with the 1st Division
notes: Event date: 17 September 1944 (Ellis, vol. II, pp. 34, 35). Event definition: On 17 September General Browning's I Airborne Corps Headquarters, in gliders, is flown in by the Royal Air Force and set up near Groesbeek; communication is established with England and with Second Army but not with the 1st or 101st Airborne Divisions; the corps commands the British 1st and the United States 82nd and 101st Airborne Divisions (pp. 27, 30 and 34-35). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. II, p. 34: "Browning's I Airborne Corps Headquarters, in gliders"; p. 35: "was flown in by the Royal Air Force and set up near Groesbeek". Location: Groesbeek, Gelderland (existing place PL0686) with a precision of 3 km. Location support: Ellis places the headquarters near Groesbeek (p. 35). Commander: Lt.-Gen. F. A. M. Browning, commanding I Airborne Corps (Ellis, vol. II, p. 30).
